reader_notes: The inference is clean and satisfying for a single-question item: the lane rejoins the turnpike well beyond the main gate, and the trust’s other two gates took what they usually took, so neither the season nor general trade explains the fall.

The “best year it took less than the yearly wage” line and the “fell by several times that wage” line are what make the key’s comparison (cost more than the bar ever took) checkable rather than merely plausible.
The detail that the two farms’ carts went through free quietly kills the distractor about the intended traffic – nicely placed, easy to miss on a fast read.
The closing line about the report not mentioning the summer is a good touch and does not affect the answer.
